Wondered what the XDC Project is I have been teasing?

Imagine you like #retrogaming and you want to play a DOS game with a friend. Both of you need to install and setup DOSBox and the game. Now you need an IPX server, you need to port forward the IPX server, you need to know your IP so that your friend can manually connect to your IPX server, and then you play. Or you rely on a website that may eventually be shut down.

If only there was a better way that is great for retro gamers, and great fun for people who use XDC compatible apps like nostr:npub1hrujuc08r4zcdtn0u6ts7u7apldcjqgftz0z7stmaaz9hwaf9jxs66f3yh (Supports Multiplayer) or right here on #Ditto (Singleplayer only for now)!

I posted this demo yesterday:
https://ditto.pub/nevent1qgsd8hjp6sy2xvyslgxyazgf8hhn4elwsme785fgd0h2tefl2ehl77cqypu9kv4z49wlzrt8fhjc57wlfcgf2wpn6qf0h3afn73trrk3jg7wgh4jcgy

But now its time to introduce XDC-DOS!

XDC-DOS is an easy way to turn almost any js-dos game into an XDC app within minutes! That's right, I didn't port that Duke Nukem game to XDC by hand. I made a tool that lets you do the same thing! And not only will this allow you to have singleplayer dos games, the IPX multiplayer works to inside compatible chat software, making this the first time you can play IPX with a friend just by pasting a file into your chat!

Making them is easy:

Step 1: Create or obtain a js-dos game (Tip, https://dos.zone has a ton of games, and if you right click the web page and choose view-source all you need to do is search that code for the .jsdos link. If its a real jsdos file its going to be more than just a few kilobytes). If you want to make them that is simple if you have dosbox knowledge, create a .jsdos folder in the folder of your game, and put a dosbox.conf inside there with the settings and the commands to automatically start the game then just zip it all up and rename it to .jsdos . You can learn more about that on js-dos.com

Step 2: Now that you have a js-dos game you can visit my website at https://xdcdos.henk.tech and upload it along with optionally a logo for the game.

Step 3: Simply click build and it will build your #webxdc app for you!

Happy gaming, and shoutout to nostr:npub16ye7evyevwnl0fc9hujsxf9zym72e063awn0pvde0huvpyec5nyq4dg4wn for both his awesome chat app and helping me test my first XDC multiplayer game.

Jungian shadow work is profound—but it is still only one chamber of the inner architecture.

The shadow contains what the conscious personality rejected: shame, fear, rage, desire, weakness, and unrealised power. Integration brings the exiled material back into relationship with the self.

Kundalini awakening, in its fullest sense, reaches deeper.

It moves through the entire embodied subconscious stack—instinct, trauma, sexuality, memory, attachment, identity, sensation, attention, and the observer who imagined itself separate from them all.

The shadow reveals what was hidden.

Kundalini reveals the machinery that hid it.

One recovers the discarded material.

The other turns the furnace inward until every layer is seen, felt, and transformed.

But intensity is not enlightenment, and heightened perception is not infallibility. The real measure is not what someone claims to have seen—it is what they can integrate without collapsing into projection, pride, or fragmentation.

The shadow asks:

What have I refused to see?

Kundalini asks:

What remains of me when nothing within can remain hidden?

This is the system I was talking about on my Nostr account.
It's the Closed Loop Ecosystem (CLE), the name I gave to the food production system I've been developing.
It's a hybrid of aquaponics, sandponics, mushroom cultivation, and composting, all working together in one closed-loop ecosystem.
No water leaves the system. Once it enters, it stays inside.
The fish are partly fed with aquatic plants grown inside the system. I still use some commercial fish feed, but my goal is to reduce that more and more over time.
This is the sandponics section.
Over here you can see the NFT channels. They don't perform very well in my climate.
Here are around 300-400 tilapia.
Further on you'll see lettuce, peppers, cabbage, duckweed, Azolla, tomatoes, mushrooms, and several other food-producing components.
The mushrooms serve two purposes: they help mineralize organic waste, making nutrients available again, and they also provide food.
The baby tilapia are bred inside the system as well.
At the moment, approximately 50% of the fish feed is produced within the system, while the remaining 50% is still commercial feed.
The entire system consumes only 235 watts of electricity.
It contains approximately 20,000 liters of water, and I only need to add around 200 liters per day, roughly 1% of the total volume.
Two additional lagoons are being built, one already completed and another almost finished.
My goal is simple:
Decentralized money + decentralized food.
Bitcoin gives us decentralized money.
The Closed Loop Ecosystem (CLE) aims to give us decentralized food production.
If you'd like to follow the development of this project, follow my account.
If you believe this work deserves more attention, please share it.
